newsitem.title: FRANCE: French kids prefer Kinder to Coke, study shows.
newsitem.headline: French kids prefer Kinder to Coke, study shows.

text.p: This year French kids prefer Kinder chocolate eggs and pocket-sized cakes to Coca-Cola, which used to take top place, a study into French children's brand preferences shows.

The study, called Kid Generation, found Kinder rocketed from fifth place in 1996 to children's first choice in 1997, pushing Coke into second slot, Joel-Yves Le Bigot, head of resarch institute L'Institut de l' Enfant which carries out the study, said on Friday.
Le Bigot told Reuters Coke's recent redesign may not appeal to the four to 10-year-olds surveyed, who tend to dislike that kind of change.
Coke may also have suffered last year from concentrating its image-building on the Olympic Games, eroding its status as a universal youth currency, he said.
"Coca-Cola's strength is its variety of references," he said.
Kinder confectionery is made by Italian family firm Ferrero.
The study, carried out every year since 1979 among mothers and children in 400 French families, also shows trends over longer periods than just one year, he said.
Over the last five to 10 years, for example, the novelty of breakfast cereals, at first greeted with enthusiasm by French children weary of their bowl of cocoa with bread and jam, has worn off.
Brands like Nestle's Chocapic and Kellogg's Chocopops have seen a decline in popularity in France, Le Bigot said.

Today's mothers show brand preferences reflecting all-round concerns for their children's activities, including sports shoe and educational toy brands, while 10 years ago they saw their role as simply feeding their children and favoured only food brands, he added.
